summary: Enhance your skills with Activity-Based Budgeting in the Public Sector training course. Learn effective budgeting techniques tailored for public sector needs.
lede: Activity-based budgeting connects public-service funding to the activities, workload and outputs that drive costs. For public finance officers, budget analysts and programme managers, it provides a way to cost services and justify resource needs using evidence. Learners practise mapping activities and cost drivers, allocating indirect costs, modelling budget scenarios and reviewing budget-to-actual variances, with principles for integrating estimates into an MTEF.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who prepare, challenge, manage, or explain public service budgets and need stronger evidence for resource allocation decisions.
prerequisites: No formal accounting qualification is required. You should have basic exposure to organizational budgets, expenditure reports, or public service planning. Working knowledge of spreadsheets is useful, but coding is not required. Advanced digital topics such as AI-assisted classification and dashboard automation are taught at conceptual and operational application level, not software-engineering level. You should bring a laptop with spreadsheet software if available; provided templates can also support the exercises.
